chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Abu Ja'far, Abu 'Abd Allah, and Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon them; and from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said:
If a thief steals from the threshing floor under a tyrannical Imam, then there is no amputation upon him; rather, he has only taken his due. But if it is under a just Imam, then upon him is killing.

key_terms.إِمَامٍ جَائِرٍ: a tyrannical ruler whose governance is unjust
key_terms.إِمَامٍ عَادِلٍ: a just ruler whose governance is legitimate and fair
key_terms.لَا قَطْعَ: no amputation penalty is to be applied
key_terms.ٱلسَّارِقُ: the thief; the person who commits theft
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْدَرِ: the threshing floor or grain collection area from which produce is taken
key_terms.ٱلْقَتْلُ: killing as the stated punishment in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stealing from the public grain store under a tyrannical or a just Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning theft from the public grain store or threshing floor in differing political conditions. It distinguishes between the rule of a tyrannical Imam and that of a just Imam, indicating that legal accountability changes according to the justice or oppression of the governing authority.
